subject: Order Form — planned operational windows & credit alignment
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order Form — planned operational windows & credit alignment

Maya — thanks for the productive call earlier. As discussed, I attached a redline of the Order Form + SLA that reflects the negotiated uptime target (99.95% monthly) and our initial service-credit table. A couple of items I want us to confirm before legal does formal signoff: 

- Planned maintenance windows: we have proposed two 4-hour weekly windows (US PST 0300–0700) that are excluded from uptime calculations; customer requested smaller windows — can you confirm the operational constraints on your side?
- Service credit scaling: we proposed a capped monthly credit equal to 30% of monthly recurring charges for the affected environment; you asked if a tiered cap would be acceptable.
- Priority response: P1 response within 1 hour, P2 within 4 hours; we can offer 24/7 on-call for P1s for Dedicated customers.

Attached: redwood_sla_redline_20260510.pdf (redline), proposed_maintenance_matrix.xlsx (ops times).

If you can confirm the maintenance window preference and whether you want a tiered cap, I’ll loop in Lauren and Aditya to propose final language for the MSA order form.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aureliahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@aureliahealth.com>, Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@aureliahealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — planned operational windows & credit alignment

Rachel — thanks for the redline. Quick answers from our side: 

- Maintenance windows: we prefer a 2-hour weekly window if possible (we have batch jobs that run early morning; minimizing the window helps downstream systems). If 2 hours is a hard blocker for your ops team, can we instead limit the weekly window to a 4-hour slot but not in the 03:00–07:00 window (our data backups run 02:00–04:00 PST)?
- Service credit cap: procurement prefers a tiered cap tied to account size. Example request: 15% cap for month-to-month usage, 25% for 12-month committed accounts, 35% for >24-month reserved capacity.
- Response times: P1 1 hour OK; please confirm that P1s include data-loss incidents and security-impacting outages.

Sarah from legal added me on the thread for precise wording. We reviewed the redline and highlighted a couple of phrasing concerns (see attached notes). Can your legal/ops propose a compromise maintenance plan and the exact maintenance exclusion clause?

Best,
Maya
Director, Cloud Operations
Aurelia Health
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, Procurement <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-13T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — planned operational windows & credit alignment

Maya — appreciate the detail. Looping in Lauren (legal ops) and Aditya (product/ops) to propose a pragmatic compromise. High level proposal from our side: 

- Maintenance windows: shift to a single 3-hour weekly window (02:30–05:30 PST) to try and avoid your 02:00–04:00 backup overlap. We’ll commit to hold non-critical changes out of the 02:30–03:30 sub-window. If that still conflicts, we can implement a maintenance blackout for your critical backup hour (02:00–03:00) and schedule the remaining 3-hour window outside that hour.
- Service credit cap: open to a tiered cap. Proposed company-side compromise: 20% cap for month-to-month, 30% for 12-month, 40% for 24+ month reserved. This keeps headroom for severe incidents while aligning incentives for longer commitments.
- P1 definition: we will align P1 to incidents that materially impact API availability (total outage for a customer environment) and security-impacting incidents. We’ll add explicit examples in the SLA.

Lauren/aditya: can you draft the exact clause language for the Order Form to reflect the maintenance exclusion and the tiered cap table?

Next steps: once we agree on wording, I’ll produce a clean Order Form and route via DocuSign.

Thanks,
Rachel
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@aureliahealth.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: maya.patel@aureliahealth.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: 2026-05-15T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — planned operational windows & credit alignment

Hi Lauren/Rachel — legal reviewed the proposed compromise and provided two small edits to ensure enforceability and auditability: 

1) Maintenance exclusion must include a requirement for advance notice (72 hours) and reasonable effort to avoid peak usage windows for the customer.
2) The credit calculation needs a clear formula: (Monthly MRC * % credit tier) prorated to the number of minutes of unavailability beyond the uptime threshold. Please include a worked example.

We are comfortable with the tiered cap you proposed (20/30/40) provided those two edits are included. We also asked procurement to confirm which commitment tier they intend to sign up for — they will circle back.

I attached a short PDF with inline comments to the redline (aurelia_sla_comments_20260515.pdf).

Regards,
Sarah Lim
Senior Counsel, Aurelia Health
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@aureliahealth.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@aureliahealth.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: 2026-05-17T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — planned operational windows & credit alignment

Thanks Sarah — we made the two edits and included a sample calculation and worked example in the attached clean Order Form (clean_order_form_20260517.docx). Highlights of language we added: 

- Maintenance exclusion: "Planned Maintenance" requires 72 hours notice and Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to avoid scheduled work during Customer-designated blackout hours; if conflict arises, Redwood will notify Customer and propose minimized-impact alternatives.
- Credit calculation: we added formula and example: Credit = (Monthly MRC) * (Credit % for tier) * (minutes of unavailability beyond threshold / total minutes in calendar month). Example included showing a 90-minute outage in a 30-day month.

Aditya — ops confirmed the 02:30–05:30 PST weekly window is feasible and that we can avoid the first hour for customers who require it. Please confirm you’ll update the maintenance matrix spreadsheet and I’ll circulate the DocuSign packet.

Maya/Procurement — once Procurement confirms commitment tier (month-to-month / 12mo / 24mo), we’ll update the order form and send for signature.

Attachments: clean_order_form_20260517.docx, proposed_maintenance_matrix.xlsx (updated).

Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal Ops
Redwood Inference
